prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” roofing company for hurricane‑rated replacements in Miami — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and needs. Instead of one name, here’s a practical way to find the best contractor for you and the specific qualifications and questions that separate true hurricane‑rated experts from general roofers.

What to require/verify
- Miami‑Dade/Florida approvals: Installers and products must meet Miami‑Dade County/Florida Building Code HVHZ requirements. Ask for Miami‑Dade/Florida Product Approval numbers or a Notice of Acceptance (NOA) for the roof system/materials.  
- Proper license and insurance: Verify the roofer’s Florida roofing contractor license (or GC license if applicable) and current liability and workers’ comp insurance. Check at Florida DBPR.  
- Manufacturer certification: Prefer contractors certified by the manufacturer (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.). This helps secure full warranties.  
- Experience with HVHZ systems: Look for documented experience with hurricane‑rated installs (metal standing seam engineered for HVHZ, Class 4 impact shingles where appropriate, properly anchored tile systems).  
- Engineering & permit handling: The contractor should get the building permit, submit engineered plans if required, and follow the fastening/attachment schedules for high wind.  
- Warranties: Get both manufacturer and workmanship warranties in writing. Ask how warranty claims are handled.  
- References & portfolio: Ask for recent Miami‑area projects, references, and photos of completed hurricane‑rated roofs.

Materials/systems commonly used for hurricane resistance
- Engineered standing‑seam metal roofing (HVHZ rated)  
- Concrete or clay tile with approved straps/anchors and proper underlayment  
- Impact‑resistant Class 4 shingles specifically listed for HVHZ installation with secondary water barrier and proper nailing pattern  
- Reinforced eave, rake, and parapet terminations, and continuous perimeter edge metal designed for uplift resistance

Key questions to ask each contractor
- “Do you have a Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval for the specific materials you’ll use?”  
- “Are you a certified installer for the manufacturer, and what warranties will I receive?”  
- “Will you pull the permit and provide engineered specifications if required?”  
- “Do you carry liability and workers’ comp insurance? Can you provide certificates?”  
- “Can you provide 3 local references for similar hurricane‑rated work?”  
- “What is the complete scope, timeline, and payment schedule? Will I receive lien waivers at payment milestones?”

How to verify them
- Florida Department of Business & Professional Regulation (DBPR) license lookup  
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control / NOA database for product and system approvals  
- Manufacturer certification lookup (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, etc.)  
- BBB, Google Reviews, Yelp, and recent homeowner references

Next step I can help with
If you share your Miami zip code or neighborhood, I can research and provide a short list (3–5) of highly rated, licensed contractors in your area that meet HVHZ requirements, with notes on certifications, reviews, and contact recommendations. Which area of Miami are you in?
